verdict.rationale: Docs show that stopping a sandbox automatically snapshots its filesystem and preserves its configuration. Retrieving a stopped sandbox by name resumes it, and persistence is the default, so the filesystem half of the story is delivered. The docs describe only filesystem and config being restored, not memory or running processes, so 'memory state intact' is unsupported. Missing for 10: evidence of memory/process-state preservation (true pause/resume of live RAM and processes), independent hands-on corroboration of resume behavior.
